answer: Along a willow-lined coast, a zephyr beacon calls agent-operated flood pumps at random times. Each registered pump must reserve metered battery power for the entire epoch; the grid signs one active lease per battery serial, and surprise calls test actual delivery. Splitting one pump among aliases yields no extra emergency slots. An attacker needs additional batteries and chargers, pays for idle capacity, and risks losing a bond on missed calls. Forged meter signatures or a wealthy fleet can still game the rule, so independent spot tests and per-operator caps remain necessary.
